2. In these revisions, Rules was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 7 dated 27-4-2022 passed by the learned Senior District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 209 of 2021 appointing two Arbitrators instead of one for the opposite parties should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Facts relevant for disposal of these Rules, in short are that, the petitioners in Civil Revision No.2150 of 2022 filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 209 of 2021 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 praying for appointment of an arbitrator for opposite party named, Amin Mohammad Foundation Limited. The opposite party appeared in the proceeding and contested the same by filing written objection. Learned District Judge after hearing both the parties, by the impugned judgment and order dated 27-4-2022 allowed the application, but appointed two arbitrators for both the parties substituting the arbitrator already nominated by the petitioners. 

 7. Mr Chowdhury Mokimuddin KJ Ali with Mr Syfuzzaman, Advocates appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 2312 of 2022 and opposite party in Civil Revision No. 2150 of 2022 submits that in appointing arbitrator under section 12 of the Arbitration Act for other party the court ought to have given opportunity to the opposite party to choose their arbitrator and suggest the name to the court, but in the instant case when the learned District Judge decided to allow the application and appoint arbitrator for the parties it was incumbent upon the court to ask the parties to the proceeding whether they have any choice in respect of appointment of arbitrator, instead of doing so the court below on its own motion, in one hand substituted the arbitrator already appointed by the petitioner by substituting one Mr Abdul Majid, Retired District and Sessions Judge and on the other hand without consent of the opposite party appointed one Md Manjurul Bashir, Retired District and Sessions Judge as arbitrator for the opposite party, as such, in both occasions the court below has committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 8. Heard the learned advocates of both the sides, have gone through the revision applications, application in Miscellaneous Case No. 209 of 2021, written objection thereto and the impugned judgment and order of the learned District Judge. 

 "THAT any sort of dispute arising between the parties during the course of implementation of the project and sale, shall be resolved by mutual discussion between the parties. In case such discussion fails, then the same shall be resolved by a board of arbitrators consisting of one representative from each party and an umpire appointed by such representatives mutually. The decisions which are to be given within 30 (thirty) days by the board of arbitrators shall be binding on both the parties. In case of the failure of the arbitrators to decide or arbitrate, it shall be decided in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and related laws of the land." 

 10. Above clause of the agreement provided that the dispute shall be resolved by a board of arbitrators consisting of one from each party and an umpire appointed by such representatives mutually. In the instant case the petitioner by a legal notice appointed Mr AF Hassan Ariff, former Advisor to the caretaker government and former Attorney-General as their arbitrator and requested the opposite party to appoint their arbitrator within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of the request, but the opposite party failed to appoint their arbitrator within time. Consequently, the petitioners filed the case praying for appointment of an arbitrator on behalf of the opposite party. The learned District Judge though allowed the application but substituted the arbitrator already nominated by the petitioners by appointing one Abdul Majid in his place which is beyond the scope of terms and conditions of deed of agreement. Law does not permit the court to substitute an arbitrator already nominated by the party unless the party prays before the court for removal or substitution of the arbitrator. Section 12 provides that the court on an application of either party to the agreement can appoint an arbitrator for and on behalf of that party who failed to appoint their arbitrator within the time given by the notice, but it cannot substitute an arbitrator already appointed.
